## 2. Sitemap URL count — before → after

| | URLs |
|---|---|
| **Before** (committed baseline, HEAD) | **597** |
| **After** (regenerated) | **561** |

**Reconciliation of the −36 net change:**

| Child sitemap | HEAD | Now | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| sitemap-locations.xml | 64 | 25 | **−39** (the 39 noindexed pages removed) |
| sitemap-products.xml | 86 | 89 | **+3** (Batch‑2 owner pages added in the same prior work) |
| all others | 447 | 447 | 0 |
| **Total** | **597** | **561** | **−36** |

- **The noindex change alone dropped the sitemap by exactly −39** (locations 64 → 25). The overall total moved 597 → 561 (net −36) because the same prior working‑tree change also **added the 3 Batch‑2 owner pages** to `sitemap-products.xml` (+3). −39 + 3 = −36. This is expected and consistent; the −39 requirement (noindex removal) is met precisely.
- Post‑regeneration composition: pages 9 + products 89 + locations 25 + blogs 438 = **561**.

## 9. Reversibility

This change is fully reversible with no data loss:

1. In each of the 39 route files, change the robots meta back from
   `content="noindex, follow"` to `content="index, follow, max-image-preview:large"`
   (the noindexed pages keep their content, canonical, and links — only the directive changed).
2. Re‑run `npm run sitemap --prefix creative-metal-industries` — the generator will
   re‑include the 39 pages automatically (it is driven purely by the robots meta, not a
   hardcoded list), restoring the sitemap to the pre‑pass URL set.
3. Re‑run `npm run build` and `npm run check:sitemap` to confirm.

No pages were deleted, no canonicals changed, no titles/styling changed. The `generate-sitemap.mjs` change (skip any route containing `content="noindex`) is generic and stays correct regardless of which pages are pruned.
